What I care about

Getting the numbers right first

Clear definitions, honest sources, and a plain note on what the data can’t tell you.

Leaving no one behind

Averages can hide the people who need attention most. I break results down by sex, age, location and income, and, where the data allow, by disability or migration status, and I check who is missing from the data.

Making it repeatable

If I can’t rerun it next month with one command, I’m not done.

Telling the story

A good chart saves the reader a page of text.

How I work

1

Question

I start with the question, not the chart.

2

Sources

I write down where the data came from and how it was defined.

3

Groups

I check who is counted, who is missing, and how groups differ.

4

Chart

I make it simple enough to read without me in the room.

5

Share

I share the code so anyone can check it.
